proposal.residence_time_basis: Liquid phase residence time (assuming gas saturation)

streams.contents: Palladium Catalyst (e.g., Pd2(dba)3 + Ligand) and Base (e.g., K2CO3 or Et3N)

proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Streams A and B are mixed first to ensure homogeneous catalyst distribution before introducing CO gas to prevent localized catalyst poisoning or precipitation. CO is introduced via a gas-liquid T-mixer immediately before the reactor coil.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas liquid streams A and B using inline degasser or sparging with inert gas to remove dissolved oxygen.
Pressurize liquid streams to >15 bar using back-pressure regulator or high-pressure pump.
Mix Stream A and Stream B in a static mixer.
Introduce Stream C (CO) via a gas-liquid T-mixer to create a segmented or homogeneous gas-liquid flow depending on pressure/velocity.
post_reactor_steps: Pass effluent through a Back-Pressure Regulator (BPR) set to 15 bar to maintain reaction pressure.
Route gas-liquid mixture to a gas-liquid separator (membrane or gravity-based) to recover unreacted CO.
Scrub recovered CO with a base trap or incinerate safely.
Collect liquid product stream for analysis.
proposal.chemistry_notes: Carbonylation reactions are sensitive to oxygen and moisture. The use of PFA tubing is critical for chemical resistance and transparency for potential visual monitoring. The high pressure (15 bar) ensures sufficient CO solubility in the organic phase. The residence time of 180 min matches the batch protocol to ensure comparable conversion.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Matched to batch protocol (3 hours) to ensure equivalent conversion.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Calculated based on reactor volume and residence time: 90 mL / 180 min = 0.5 mL/min.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Set to 15 bar to match batch pressure and ensure CO solubility.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Coiled tubing is standard for high-pressure gas-liquid reactions due to ease of heating and pressure containment.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA is chemically inert to organic solvents, bases, and CO, and can withstand 15 bar at 100 C.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID provides a good balance between pressure drop and mixing efficiency for gas-liquid flow.

reasoning_per_field.safety_flags: CO is toxic. Ensure all connections are leak-tight. Use a CO detector in the lab. Vent gas exhaust to a scrubber or incinerator. High pressure (15 bar) requires rated fittings and tubing.
